Hacker News and GitHub captures are external_signal; they never make a brief area decision_ready. Only a captured public web page counts as external_evidence.
The decision brief emits external_signal basis rows and the task-input contract accepts them; tests/harness/test_intelligence.py validates a signal-only brief against the schema.

scripts/check_release_gate.py verifies declared commits are ancestors of HEAD, requires head_relation when head_commit differs from HEAD, checks that the declared post-verification paths exactly match the diff, and compares catalog revisions plus tracked-file and test counts; wired into validate.yml and harness.yml

benchmark.note: Quality is the deterministic rubric score out of 100. It checks structure, traceability and completeness only; it is not a model-quality or business-quality score.

known_limitations: No real-model V1.0 vs V1.1 comparison was run in this pass; model quality and token cost are NOT TESTED.
Structural benchmark scores do not measure commercial quality.
Hacker News points and comments are public discussion activity, not demand, adoption, paying customers or market size.
Competitive and market sections in the exported package only use captured sources; when none exist the package says so instead of inventing numbers.
There is no independent semantic reviewer; verbatim quote matches stay unverified.
Real publishing, outreach, CRM writes, ad spend and customer outcomes are not executed or measured.
Capture verification is structural: a fabricated local web capture with a plausible hash is not detected without re-fetching the page.
The exported package groups mapped claims as external_evidence even when the decision brief labels the source external_signal.
docs/product-scope.md lives on this Draft branch; if PR #3 is not merged, the scope document is not on main.
